info.bio:
There are many artists with the name Green:

1. A rap artist (Adam Ciesielski) from Łódź, Poland. He has released two albums, Kryptonim Monolog (2010) and Buntownicy I Lojaliści (2013).
He was in groups Phonoloftaleina and Popkiller Młode Wilki, and sometimes works under the name Greenzki.

2. A power pop band from Chicago, USA. It was formed in 80s by guitarist/singer/songwriter Jeff Lescher, whose influences included the Kinks, T. Rex, and soul music.

scenes.name: College-pop y nacimiento del lo-fi
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La población universitaria del Sur adopta la ética de la new wave y la adapta a la melodía: un pop inusualmente intelectual, con raíces en el folk-rock y el country-rock pero contaminado por las neurosis de la época. Athens (Georgia) compite con las capitales del rock: B-52's y R.E.M., uno de los grupos de más éxito de la historia. Carolina del Norte (dB's, Windbreakers), Hoboken (Smithereens, Bongos, Tiny Lights), el nacimiento del lo-fi (Half Japanese, Violent Femmes, Beat Happening, Guided By Voices, Sebadoh), They Might Be Giants, Green, B.A.L.L., Boston (Volcano Suns, 10,000 Maniacs, Throwing Muses, Blake Babies), la Costa Oeste (Game Theory, Posies, Young Fresh Fellows) y la sátira de Ween.

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …the format of the jam session from jazz music, but the atmosphere from Ernst's surrealistic paintings, horror soundtracks and voodoo rituals, Green indulged in sheer sound-painting. The hallucinated ramble of the guitar weaves colorful textures for mantra-like psalms. It is visceral, primordial…

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …Document (1987) revealed their melodic talent with a cornucopia of catchy hooks: The One I Love, Finest Worksong, This Is The End Of The World, etc. Green (1988) was another incredible batch of pop songs (including Stand and Orange Crush), but hardly a cohesive unit: it had the feeling of a compilation…

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …less encyclopedic. Chicago's Green (12) were among the great unsung heroes of the 1980s. The quantity and quality of elements that concurred to make Green (1986) a phantasmagoric song cycle had few rivals: one could hear echoes of Buddy Holly, Ray Charles, Marvin Gaye, Kinks, Rolling Stones, Hollies,…
